label: Simulation of a material
summary: A model of a material, a set of rules and a list of questions answered on a computer.

label: Materials from atoms
summary: A material is a crowd of nuclei with electrons that decide bonding, conduction and colour.

label: Quantum mechanics for electrons
summary: The rules that describe electrons, which are too light for everyday ball-and-spring physics.

label: The ladder of methods
summary: Simulation methods trade accuracy against cost, from force fields to exact solutions.

label: Cost scaling
summary: How much more work a method needs when the system grows.

label: What DFT can and cannot tell you
summary: The questions DFT answers well, with care, or not at all.

label: The ground state
summary: The lowest-energy arrangement of the electrons for a given set of atoms.

label: Roadmap to a first project
summary: The order in which to learn the ideas, the settings and the checks.

label: The VASP workflow
summary: Four input files, one command, and output files to read and check.

label: Wave nature of electrons
summary: Electrons show interference, so they have a wavelength that depends on momentum.

label: Meaning of the wavefunction
summary: The square of the wavefunction gives the probability of finding the electron near a point.

label: Quantization in a box
summary: Only waves that fit between the walls are allowed, so energies come in steps.

label: Orbital shapes
summary: The s, p, d and f shapes and the quantum numbers that label them.

label: Spin and the Pauli principle
summary: Each orbital holds two electrons of opposite spin, and no two share a state.

label: From levels to bands
summary: Many atoms turn single levels into bands, separated by gaps.

label: The many-electron problem
summary: Electrons repel each other, so their motions are tied together.

label: The exponential wall
summary: The exact problem multiplies in size with every added electron.

label: Electron density
summary: A map of how much electron charge sits at each point, with three variables only.

label: From density to potential
summary: The ground-state density fixes the external potential, up to a constant.

label: Why approximations are needed
summary: The exact functional is unknown, so one term must be approximated.

label: Hohenberg-Kohn theorems
summary: The two theorems that make the density a sufficient variable.

label: Variational principle
summary: The true ground-state density gives the lowest energy among all trial densities.

label: The Kohn-Sham idea
summary: Replace the interacting electrons by non-interacting ones that share the same density.

label: Kohn-Sham equations
summary: One-electron equations whose effective potential depends on the density.

label: Exchange-correlation term
summary: The one energy term that is not known exactly and must be approximated.

label: The self-consistent loop
summary: Guess a density, solve, update, and repeat until input and output agree.

label: Density mixing
summary: How the new density is blended with the old one to keep the loop stable.

label: Kohn-Sham eigenvalues
summary: The energies of the auxiliary system and what they do and do not mean.

label: Plane waves as a basis
summary: Wavefunctions in a crystal are written as a sum of waves with set wavelengths.

label: Bloch theorem
summary: In a repeating crystal, each wavefunction is a plane wave times a repeating part.

label: Reciprocal space
summary: The space of wave vectors, with its own repeating cell.

label: Plane-wave cutoff
summary: The largest wave energy kept in the basis, which controls accuracy and cost.

label: Brillouin zone
summary: The primitive cell of reciprocal space.

label: k-point sampling
summary: Integrals over the Brillouin zone are replaced by a finite set of points.

label: k-point meshes
summary: Regular grids of k-points, and when a Gamma-centred grid is the safer choice.

label: Pseudopotentials
summary: A smooth stand-in for the nucleus and core electrons.

label: The PAW method
summary: Projector augmented waves recover the true wavefunction near the core.

label: Choosing a functional
summary: The ladder of exchange-correlation approximations and their typical strengths.

label: Hybrid functionals
summary: Functionals that mix in part of the Hartree-Fock exchange, at higher cost.

label: van der Waals corrections
summary: Corrections for the weak attraction that simple functionals miss.

label: Smearing
summary: Fractional occupations near the Fermi level that help metals converge.

label: Spin polarization
summary: Letting spin-up and spin-down electrons differ, needed for magnetic materials.

label: DFT+U
summary: An on-site correction for strongly interacting localized electrons.

label: Lattice and structure
summary: A crystal is a repeating cell described by three vectors and the atom positions in it.

label: The POSCAR file
summary: The structure input: cell, species and atomic positions.

label: The KPOINTS file
summary: The input that sets how the Brillouin zone is sampled.

label: The INCAR file
summary: The input of tags that control what is calculated and how carefully.

label: The POTCAR file
summary: The licensed pseudopotential input; this site never shows its contents.

label: Job scripts
summary: The batch script that asks a cluster to run the calculation.

label: OUTCAR and OSZICAR
summary: The output files, and which lines to read first.

label: Restarting from earlier results
summary: Reusing a wavefunction or charge density from a previous run.

label: Convergence testing
summary: Raising a setting until the quantity you care about stops changing.

label: Cutoff convergence
summary: Testing the plane-wave cutoff against the quantity of interest.

label: k-point convergence
summary: Testing the k-point mesh against the quantity of interest.

label: Common errors and fixes
summary: Typical failures, what they mean, and how to correct them.

label: Total energy
summary: The energy of the electrons and nuclei, useful for comparing structures.

label: Forces and relaxation
summary: Moving atoms along the forces until the structure is stable.

label: Density of states
summary: How many electron states sit at each energy.

label: Band structure
summary: Energies of the states along a path through the Brillouin zone.

label: Charge density analysis
summary: Looking at where the electrons sit in a calculated material.

label: Elastic constants
summary: How the energy changes when the cell is deformed.

label: Optical properties
summary: Estimating absorption from the computed states, with known limits.

label: The perovskite structure
summary: The ABX3 family of crystals built from corner-sharing octahedra.

label: Tolerance factors
summary: Heuristic ratios of ionic radii that hint at whether a perovskite can form.

label: A worked perovskite workflow
summary: A full relaxation, SCF and band-structure run on an example oxide.

label: Material Builder
summary: Building and editing structures before a calculation.

label: Screening studies
summary: Running many related calculations and comparing results with care.

label: Born-Oppenheimer approximation
summary: Treat the heavy nuclei as fixed while the light electrons are solved for.

label: Fermi level
summary: The energy up to which states are filled at zero temperature.

label: Symmetry and space groups
summary: The symmetry operations of a crystal, which reduce work and fix allowed paths.

label: Supercells
summary: Repeated copies of a cell, used to describe defects and larger patterns.

label: Ionic radii
summary: Tabulated sizes of ions that depend on charge and coordination.
